lines: A chunk of the space station fell out of the sky and smashed straight through a family's roof in Florida.
It came from a load of old batteries, heavier than a pickup truck, that NASA tossed overboard three years earlier.
The whole thing was supposed to burn up on the way down. One piece didn't.
It tore through the roof and two floors, with their son at home, and it was smaller than a soda can.
NASA admitted it was theirs. Now the family wants NASA to pay for the house. Should they?
